transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Lin (Redwood Partnerships), Carlos (Velascale), Priya (Velascale Product), Ethan (Velascale Infra), Sara (Velascale Security)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to meet you all. quick agenda - intro, partnership models, technical fit, next steps.
[00:18] Carlos: yeah thanks, Maya, excited to chat. Velascale basically runs a distributed GPU infra, we do colocation and cloud, we want to understand how Redwood sees partners for Dedicated and private offerings.
[00:32] Owen: cool, i'll jump in for the technical piece, but high level: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private deployments in customer VPCs or on-prem. we see partners providing GPU capacity and infra, and integrations are typically around API routing, billing integration, and optionally a managed cluster for Dedicated.
[00:50] Priya: quick q - are you expecting partners to run your control plane or just the compute?
[01:03] Lin: good q. we usually keep the control plane hosted for speed of ops for hosted customers, but for Private deployments we can do a customer-controlled control plane or a partner-managed option depending on the contract. sometimes customers want an air-gapped on-prem install.
[01:22] Ethan: from infra standpoint, we care about latency, KV cache locality, and how the runtime uses multi-gpu for batching. do you have any specific kernel or driver constraints?
[01:38] Owen: runtime is fairly flexible; we optimize kernel selection for architecture and sequence length. for NVLink topologies we optimize KV cache and sharding. H100 vs A100 differences affect quantization and perf; we can share profiles.
[01:55] Carlos: what about billing and quotas - can partners surface usage to end customers?
[02:08] Maya: yes, two models - partner resell (we invoice partner, partner invoices end customer) or partner as infra provider with cross-account routing. we also support SSO/SAML and RBAC for multi-tenant partners.
[02:24] Sara: security - SOC 2, audit logs, and KMS. we need to see how keys are handled if Redwood control plane is used vs partner-managed.
[02:38] Owen: for kms we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via standard key-wrapping; when control plane is hosted by Redwood we support envelope encryption and can integrate with partner KMS via federated access. we will send the security docs.
[02:56] Priya: are there size minimums for Dedicated? customers expect predictable throughput, so they'd consider reserved capacity.
[03:10] Maya: yes we have reserved capacity packages, typical commitments vary but we can be flexible for strategic partners - usually monthly or annual commits with burst policies.
[03:26] Carlos: ok, can we talk about runbook for benchmarks? we want to show customers Redwood on Velascale infra with H100 clusters.
[03:40] Owen: sure, typical benchmark: sample prompt set (few-shot chat + long-context generation), sequence lengths, steady-state throughput, p99 latency. we do both multi-query throughput and single-stream latency. we can provide harness scripts and test data.
[03:58] Ethan: what about model variants - do you require specific model formats? ONNX? torchscript?
[04:12] Owen: we support standard transformer checkpoints and common runtimes; we do prefer quantized formats for cost/perf optimization but can ingest full fp16/fp32. kernel selection works at runtime. occasionally transcription here tends to flip product names but essentially if it's a transformer checkpoint we're good.
[04:33] Carlos: are there any restrictions on GPUs? we also support custom boards and non-NVIDIA GPUs for edge.
[04:46] Owen: Redwood's runtime is optimized for NVIDIA right now (A100/H100 families) but we have partners experimenting with other accelerators; for the initial integration let's focus on H100/A100.
[04:59] Maya: for go-to-market, we usually propose a joint benchmark, then a pilot Dedicated offering for one or two anchor customers, followed by co-marketing.
[05:12] Lin: also co-sell credits and a partner portal - we can discuss partner tiering (silver/gold/platinum) and revenue share models.
[05:26] Priya: what's the expected timeline for a pilot if we run a benchmark next week?
[05:36] Maya: benchmark week -> 1-2 weeks of validation -> pilot onboarding ~4-6 weeks depending on security review and infra provisioning.
[05:46] Sara: speaking of security review, we'll need SOC2 docs, pen test summary, and details on audit logs retention. can you share those?
[05:58] Owen: yes we'll share SOC2 report redacted, and a security FAQ. also we support configurable audit log retention in Redwood Console.
[06:12] Carlos: can we see a sample contract / pricing? even ballpark for partner-resell vs infra provider?
[06:24] Maya: absolutely, I'll send a partner pricing matrix - ballpark numbers and typical margins; final pricing depends on commit size and term.
[06:35] Ethan: one technical thing - our infra uses Kubernetes with custom device plugin; how tightly does Redwood depend on that? will we need to run a special agent?
[06:48] Owen: we have a lightweight agent for scheduling and telemetry; for Dedicated we can integrate with k8s device plugins or run our own orchestration layer. agent is optional if you prefer a managed cluster.
[07:01] Carlos: great. do you have any reference partners we can talk to?
[07:08] Lin: yes, we can share two partner references who've run Dedicated on partner infra. I'll include contact details in the playbook.
[07:17] [minor crosstalk] Priya: sorry - quick question, do you support model pinning and rollout for multi-tenant?
[07:25] Owen: yes, rollout policies, canary, A/B tests, automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained.
[07:33] Sara: one more - data residency & logs: some customers need logs to stay within region, possible?
[07:42] Maya: yes, for Private deployments we support region-restricted logging and data residency. for hosted we also have region controls but partner-managed infra gives more control.
[07:55] Carlos: ok let's recap next steps.
[08:02] Maya: recap - Redwood to share playbook + security docs, Owen to prepare benchmark harness, propose dates for SE deep dive, Velascale to share infra topology and security constraints.
[08:14] Priya: works for us. any potential blockers? budget or legal?
[08:22] Carlos: legal will need to look at contract, but not a blocker.
[08:27] Maya: great. we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. thanks everyone.

[End of call]

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels may be generic and product names occasionally garbled; audio was clear but multiple speakers overlapped briefly.
notes: Call felt like a productive intro; Velascale interested in H100 benchmarks and a pilot. Security is main gating item. Redwood AE/SE pair present. Agreed next steps and owners.
